chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Sindy, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'at, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Fear God regarding the two weak ones, meaning the orphan and the women.
ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet's family mean by the 'two weak ones' in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) linking piety (*taqwa*) specifically to the rights of orphans and women, reflecting the Quranic emphasis on social justice. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view that caring for these 'weak ones' is not merely charitable but a core component of comprehensive faith and societal stability.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-13 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibnAhmad, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Sindy, on the authority of Uthman ibn Isa, on the authority of Sama’at, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “
Fear God regarding two weak ones meaning orphans and women.”
